description: Empirical reasoning schemas and archetypes for baseline JavaScript runtime mechanics and TypeScript type safety (U01 to U07).

archetypes.name: Defensive Primitive Sanitization & Coercion Guard
archetypes.coreConcept: Distinguishing primitive types from reference values, enforcing strict equality, and handling nullish values (null/undefined) safely without overwriting legitimate falsy values (0, false, empty string).
mentalModel: 1. Identify whether incoming properties are primitive values (number, string, boolean) or missing (null, undefined).
2. Use strict equality (===) and nullish coalescing (??) instead of logical OR (||) to preserve legitimate 0 or false values.
3. Return sanitized data transfer object conforming to the schema specification.
archetypes.governingInvariant: sanitizedValue = (inputVal !== null && inputVal !== undefined) ? inputVal : defaultValue

cognitiveTraps.name: Falsy Zero Value Overwrite
cognitiveTraps.description: Using 'val || defaultVal' overwrites valid 0 or empty string with default values.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Pass { timeoutSec: 0 }; with || default of 30, it incorrectly yields 30 instead of 0.

cognitiveTraps.name: Loose Equality Implicit Coercion
cognitiveTraps.description: Comparing with '==' causes unintended coercion between false, 0, and empty strings.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Comparing '' == 0 returns true, bypassing empty string validation.

realWorldDomains.description: Sanitizing environment variable overrides for microservice configuration.
Normalizing user settings where 0 or false are valid operational thresholds.

qualityChecks.check: Defaults use `??` or an explicit `null`/`undefined` check, never `||`.
qualityChecks.why: `||` overwrites legitimate falsy values such as `0`, `false`, and `''` with the default.

qualityChecks.check: Empty-string or missing-number checks test `=== ''` or `Number.isFinite(...)` explicitly rather than truthiness (`!val`).
qualityChecks.why: Truthiness checks conflate `0` and `''` with `null` or `undefined`.

archetypes.name: Encapsulated Lexical Scope & Closure State Factory
archetypes.coreConcept: Creating private state enclosed within execution context boundaries, exposing controlled accessors without leaking internal data structures.
mentalModel: 1. Initialize private state variables inside the outer factory function frame.
2. Return an object interface whose methods form closures over the private state.
3. Ensure external mutation cannot compromise internal state references.
archetypes.governingInvariant: privateState accessible exclusively through returned accessor functions; outer lexical frame retained in heap

cognitiveTraps.name: Internal Reference Escape
cognitiveTraps.description: Returning a direct reference to an internal mutable array or object allows external mutation bypassing encapsulation.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Call state.getAll(); mutate returned array; internal registry is corrupted without calling add().

realWorldDomains.description: Thread-safe event counter tracking request latency buckets and hit counts.
In-memory token vault holding ephemeral credentials with controlled expiration.

qualityChecks.check: Accessors returning internal arrays or objects return a shallow copy or freeze, never the live internal reference.
qualityChecks.why: Returning the internal reference lets callers mutate private closure state outside the factory API.

qualityChecks.check: Mutable state lives in `let`/`const` bindings inside the factory closure rather than as properties on the returned object.
qualityChecks.why: Storing state on the returned object exposes it to direct external reassignment.

archetypes.name: Immutable Collection Transformation Pipeline
archetypes.coreConcept: Processing and summarizing datasets using pure transformation pipelines (map, filter, reduce) without mutating input collections.
mentalModel: 1. Filter input records by required business status or timestamp range.
2. Map/transform matching records into normalized reporting schemas.
3. Reduce into structured aggregations (grouping by key, summing totals, computing percentiles).

cognitiveTraps.name: In-Place Array Sort Mutation
cognitiveTraps.description: Calling Array.prototype.sort() directly on input array mutates the original order unexpectedly.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Call sortOrders(orders); check original orders array order; order was permanently altered.

realWorldDomains.description: Aggregating daily settlement revenue by category with tax breakdowns.
Summarizing microservice error counts grouped by HTTP response code.

qualityChecks.check: Sorting or reversing a caller-owned array uses `[...arr].sort(...)` or `toSorted()`, never `arr.sort()` directly.
qualityChecks.why: `Array.prototype.sort` and `reverse` mutate the array in place and corrupt the caller's ordering.

qualityChecks.check: Every `.reduce(...)` call passes an explicit initial accumulator value as its second argument.
qualityChecks.why: Omitting the initial value throws a `TypeError` on empty arrays and reuses the first element as the accumulator.

archetypes.name: DOM Event Delegation & Propagation Controller
archetypes.coreConcept: Managing dynamic UI interactions via parent delegation, accounting for event bubbling from nested child elements (e.g. icons, spans inside buttons), and preventing event propagation issues.
mentalModel: 1. Attach a single listener to the container element rather than each child row.
2. On event trigger, traverse upward using event.target.closest(selector) to match the interactive boundary.
3. Ensure clicks on nested children (icons, bold tags) trigger the correct handler with the parent dataset attributes.
archetypes.governingInvariant: delegatedTarget = event.target.closest('[data-action]'); handler executed with target dataset attributes

cognitiveTraps.name: Direct Target Assumption on Nested Elements
cognitiveTraps.description: Inspecting event.target.dataset directly instead of event.target.closest('[data-action]') fails when clicking inner <span> or <i>.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Simulate click with event.target = <span> nested inside <button data-action='delete'>; target.dataset is empty.

realWorldDomains.description: Handling row action buttons (edit, delete, view) in high-throughput virtualized data tables.
Managing interactive task card interactions across dynamic columns.

qualityChecks.check: Delegated event handlers locate the interactive element via `event.target.closest(selector)` rather than reading `event.target` directly.
qualityChecks.why: Clicking a nested `<span>` or icon inside a button sets `event.target` to the child, missing the parent's `dataset`.

qualityChecks.check: The result of `event.target.closest(selector)` is checked for `null` before reading properties.
qualityChecks.why: Clicks on non-matching container areas return `null` from `closest()`, throwing a `TypeError` if dereferenced.

archetypes.name: Resilient Async Microtask & Promise Combinator
archetypes.coreConcept: Orchestrating concurrent asynchronous operations with partial failure tolerance, microtask coordination, and deterministic timeout aborts.
mentalModel: 1. Accept an array of asynchronous tasks and execute them concurrently.
2. Isolate failures so that individual task rejections do not abort surviving tasks.
3. Return structured settlement results partitioned into fulfilled values and rejected errors.
archetypes.governingInvariant: results.length === tasks.length; all promises settled before resolving combinator

cognitiveTraps.name: Premature Fast-Fail with Promise.all
cognitiveTraps.description: Using Promise.all for independent tasks causes a single transient failure to abort all other valid results.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: 3 tasks run; task 2 fails; results of task 1 and 3 are lost.

realWorldDomains.description: Aggregating upstream service dependency health checks with per-service latency.
Preloading critical UI assets in parallel with graceful fallbacks.

qualityChecks.check: Independent concurrent tasks use `Promise.allSettled` (or per-task `try/catch`), never bare `Promise.all`.
qualityChecks.why: `Promise.all` rejects on the first failure and discards the results of all other surviving tasks.

qualityChecks.check: Combinator results are returned in the same positional order as the input `tasks` array.
qualityChecks.why: Pushing into a result array inside `.then()` callbacks reorders results by completion time instead of input order.

archetypes.name: Discriminated Union & State Machine Reducer
archetypes.coreConcept: Implementing strict runtime and compile-time state transitions using discriminated union action patterns and type narrowing guards, enforcing exhaustive coverage without unhandled branches.
mentalModel: 1. Define distinct states and event actions characterized by a common discriminant property (e.g. 'type' or 'status').
2. In the transition reducer, narrow action payload types based on the discriminant.
3. Reject invalid state-to-state transitions with descriptive domain errors, guaranteeing state consistency.
archetypes.governingInvariant: newState = transition(currentState, action); invalid transitions throw InvalidStateTransitionError

cognitiveTraps.name: State Mutation on Invalid Transition
cognitiveTraps.description: Permitting transition actions from incompatible states (e.g. CANCELLED -> SHIPPED) corrupts domain state integrity.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Dispatch PAY event on an already REFUNDED order; status changes to COMPLETED.

realWorldDomains.description: Managing e-commerce payment checkout flow (INITIAL -> AUTHORIZED -> CAPTURED / VOIDED).
Enforcing device firmware update lifecycle (IDLE -> DOWNLOADING -> VERIFYING -> FLASHING).

qualityChecks.check: Invalid state-to-action transitions throw an explicit domain error rather than silently returning the old state or mutating it.
qualityChecks.why: Silent fallthrough masks illegal transitions such as shipping a cancelled order.

qualityChecks.check: Switch or branch chains over a discriminated union include a `default` branch that throws on unknown discriminants.
qualityChecks.why: A missing `default` branch lets newly added action types fall through silently.

qualityChecks.check: State transitions return a new state object instead of reassigning `state.status` or payload fields in place.
qualityChecks.why: Mutating the current state object breaks reducer predictability and corrupts prior snapshots.

archetypes.name: Diagnostic Debugging & Minimal Reproducer Isolation
archetypes.coreConcept: Locating and remediating subtle logical bugs and boundary defects in existing code guided by reproducer test suites without causing regressions.
mentalModel: 1. Run test suite to observe exact assertion failure and reproducer input.
2. Trace variable state changes step-by-step through the defective execution path.
3. Apply targeted remediation preserving external function signature and existing behavior.
archetypes.governingInvariant: failing reproducer test turns Green; all existing baseline tests remain Green

cognitiveTraps.name: Special-Case Patching Instead of Root-Cause Fix
cognitiveTraps.description: Adding an ad-hoc if statement for the specific test case rather than fixing the underlying logical equation.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Add 'if (x === 42) return true;' passing test 1 but failing boundary test with x = 43.

realWorldDomains.description: Fixing URL query string serializer for repeated keys and special character encoding.
Fixing deep object path getter ('a.b.c') when encountering null or intermediate primitives.

qualityChecks.check: The fix addresses the underlying condition or invariant rather than hardcoding an `if` branch for a specific test input.
qualityChecks.why: Special-casing a single reproducer input leaves the root bug intact for all other boundary values.

qualityChecks.check: The exported function name, parameter order, and return shape match the original contract without breaking baseline callers.
qualityChecks.why: Changing the public signature or return type breaks existing callers and regression tests.

archetypes.name: Function Parameters: Defaults, Rest Arguments & Numeric Rounding
archetypes.coreConcept: A function signature controls how missing and variable-length arguments arrive: default parameters apply only when an argument is undefined, rest parameters collect any number of trailing arguments into an array, and money values must be rounded explicitly.
mentalModel: 1. Decide which parameters are required, which have defaults, and which are variadic.
2. Use a default parameter (rate = 0.1) instead of `rate || 0.1`, so an explicit 0 is respected.
3. Collect variadic inputs with a rest parameter (...items) and reduce them with an explicit initial value.
4. Round the final number once, at the end, to the required decimal places and return a number, not a string.
archetypes.governingInvariant: f(a) === f(a, defaultValue) && f(a, 0) applies 0; restArgs.reduce(sum, 0) === 0 when no arguments are passed

cognitiveTraps.name: Falsy Argument Replaced by Default
cognitiveTraps.description: Using `arg || default` replaces a deliberate 0 with the default value.

cognitiveTraps.name: Reduce Without Initial Value
cognitiveTraps.description: Calling reduce on an empty rest array without an initial value throws a TypeError.

cognitiveTraps.name: toFixed Returns a String
cognitiveTraps.description: Returning `value.toFixed(2)` yields a string, so strict equality with a number fails.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: applyDiscount(19.99) === 17.99 is false because the result is '17.99'.

realWorldDomains.description: Applying optional promotional rates at checkout.
Summing a variable number of invoice lines with tax.

qualityChecks.check: Optional parameters use ES default parameters (`param = defaultVal`) or `??`, never `param || defaultVal`.
qualityChecks.why: `param || defaultVal` discards explicit `0` or `false` arguments passed by the caller.

qualityChecks.check: Rest parameter reductions (`...items`) supply an explicit initial value (such as `0`) so zero trailing arguments do not throw.
qualityChecks.why: Calling `.reduce()` without an initial value on an empty rest array throws a `TypeError`.

qualityChecks.check: Monetary or decimal results are rounded numerically (`Math.round(x * 100) / 100` or `Number(x.toFixed(2))`) and returned as a `number`, never a `toFixed` string.
qualityChecks.why: `toFixed()` returns a string, which breaks numeric arithmetic and strict equality checks.

archetypes.name: Array & Object Basics: Aggregation, Filtering, Nested Access & Immutable Updates
archetypes.coreConcept: Arrays and objects are reference values: read nested fields deliberately, derive new collections with map/filter/reduce, and return new objects or arrays instead of mutating the caller's data.
mentalModel: 1. Identify the input shape (array of numbers, array of objects, nested object, or key-value map).
2. Derive results with non-mutating operations (filter, map, reduce, spread) rather than sort/splice/assignment on the input.
3. For key-value maps, read missing keys with a fallback (?? 0) and write into a copy ({ ...obj, [key]: value }).
4. Format output exactly as specified, including singular/plural wording and rounding.
archetypes.governingInvariant: deepEqual(inputBefore, inputAfter) && output satisfies the specified shape

cognitiveTraps.name: Mutating the Caller's Data
cognitiveTraps.description: Sorting the input array or assigning into the input object changes data the caller still uses.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: adjustStock(stock, 'SKU-1', 2) also changes stock['SKU-1'] in the caller.

cognitiveTraps.name: Missing Key Produces NaN
cognitiveTraps.description: Adding a delta to an undefined map entry yields NaN instead of starting from 0.

cognitiveTraps.name: Output Not Normalized
cognitiveTraps.description: Forgetting to round, trim or lowercase derived values, or to switch to the singular form.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: buildShippingLabel with one item returns '(1 items)'.

realWorldDomains.description: Summarizing sensor readings without altering the raw series.
Exporting normalized emails of active subscribers.
Formatting labels from nested order data.
Applying stock adjustments immutably.

qualityChecks.check: Updating a key-value map creates a new object (`{ ...map, [key]: next }`) rather than assigning to `inputMap[key]`.
qualityChecks.why: Assigning to `inputMap[key]` mutates the caller's object in place.

qualityChecks.check: Reading an optional or missing object key for arithmetic uses `?? 0` before adding or incrementing.
qualityChecks.why: Adding a number to `undefined` produces `NaN` and corrupts the map entry.

qualityChecks.check: String normalization (`.trim()`, `.toLowerCase()`) and singular/plural branches are applied explicitly before returning formatted output.
qualityChecks.why: Unnormalized whitespace or hardcoded plural suffixes produce mismatched labels on edge inputs.
